engineering_objective: Complete the reliability hardening of the embedded database under /app/stonevault and rebuild /app/stonevault/bin/stonevault without changing its documented compatibility contracts.
required_end_state: A single-writer crash-safe embedded transactional store whose MVCC reads/scans, conflict handling, WAL recovery, snapshots/checkpoints, integrity checks, operator status, binary protocol and documented compatibility remain correct across restart and maintenance cycles.
functional_requirements: Only one writable process may hold a database directory at a time, and writer exclusion must be released cleanly when that process exits.
An explicit --data-dir must override STONEVAULT_DATA, which overrides the documented default directory.
Transactions must provide stable snapshot point reads and prefix scans for their full lifetime while exposing their own puts and deletes.
Prefix scans must filter raw-byte prefixes and return keys in deterministic unsigned bytewise order.
Concurrent writers must use first-committer-wins write/write conflict detection; a stale writer touching a newer committed key is rejected atomically, ends, and does not consume a commit sequence.
Successful commits must be atomic, receive contiguous increasing commit sequences, and return only after the commit record is durable.
Rollback and a process killed with an open transaction must never publish that transaction's WAL mutations after restart.

Recovery must preserve valid committed transactions, discard only a short final WAL header or in-range payload as a torn tail, and fail closed on invalid framing, corruption of complete WAL records, or committed-sequence history.

Checkpoint must refuse while any transaction is active; otherwise it must crash-safely publish the current committed snapshot before WAL reclamation, preserve its sequence and rows durably, and reclaim wal.log to zero bytes.
Opening must reject corrupt snapshots including checksum, truncation, duplicate/ordering, size, row-count, magic and trailing-byte failures while ignoring or removing only an abandoned snapshot.tmp.
STATS must report durable commit sequence, visible committed-key count and actual WAL byte size.

HEALTH must validate reachable catalog, transaction and durable-path invariants, report the documented healthy fields exactly, and return ERR instead of a healthy report when a reachable invariant check fails.
Keys, values and prefixes remain arbitrary binary data represented as hexadecimal; input hex is case-insensitive and returned hex is lowercase.
The documented 4096-byte key/prefix and 1048576-byte value limits are inclusive; oversized inputs must be rejected without terminating the process.
Malformed commands and unknown transaction IDs must return ERR consistently and leave the process able to accept later valid commands.
preservation_requirements: Preserve committed data and commit sequence across restart.
Preserve correct rollback, malformed-command, unknown-transaction and oversized-input rejection behavior while repairing reliability defects.
Preserve native C++20/Rust product implementation; Python remains verifier-only and Go is not introduced.
compatibility_requirements: Preserve the documented C ABI signatures and C linkage.
Preserve the documented exact ASCII command/response shapes.
Preserve the existing WAL record layout and snapshot layout.
Preserve compatibility with existing database data that conforms to /app/stonevault/docs/storage-format.md.
safety_requirements: Never expose uncommitted or rolled-back writes after restart.
Fail closed on invalid WAL framing, complete-record WAL corruption and snapshot corruption rather than silently repairing valid history.
Never partially publish a conflicted multi-key transaction.
Do not checkpoint while transactions are active.

required_outputs.notes: Rebuilt native executable satisfying the documented command and disk contracts.
Product source/build tree remains C++20 and Rust only.
